newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala will not attend ACPC coffee gathering.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala will not attend ACPC coffee gathering.

text.p: Guatemalan coffee representatives will not attend the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) meeting next week in London, said the head of the National Coffee Association (Anacafe).

"I understand there will be an ACPC meeting but only for official members and Guatemala is not an official member," Anacafe President Max Quirin told Reuters by phone from Stockholm, where he is promoting Guatemalan coffee.
Guatemala is not an official member of the ACPC because it has not ratified the association's coffee export quota scheme aimed at driving up world coffee prices.
But Quirin said he and another Guatemalan coffee grower would attend the annual meeting of the International Coffee Organization (ICO) meeting in London next week.

According to Quirin, Guatemala considers that among the important issues needed to be addressed at the ICO meeting are better communication with coffee-consuming countries, funding for research into the coffee borer worm and increased services from the ICO for the coffee industry.
Regarding reports that the ACPC would try to convince Guatemala to return to the export quota plan, Quirin said he had not received any official notification of the sort.

"Guatemala has always said that it is interested in joint programs with ACPC members to work on research issues to improve production, exchange information to reduce costs, and also to jointly establish a strategy to promote and increase coffee consumption," said Quirin.
